genre: Cozy merge puzzle with home-restoration and collection meta
title: Merge Bazaar: Festival Homes
audience: Women 25-55 in India, Southeast Asia and diaspora, plus global cozy-merge players who want unhurried, story-led play. Secondary: families who play together on one device.
controls: Touch only. Drag an item onto an identical item (or group) to merge. A long-press shows the merge preview before release: count, resulting item and tier. Tap a generator to produce, tap a crate to open it, and tap an item to select it, which highlights valid targets. Drag an item to the order tray to fill an order. Drag an item to the Bag (a 12-slot storage strip below the board that also extends from the home screen) to store it. Tap the Sort button to auto-arrange the board by chain and tier. Sort never merges and never touches locked or blocked tiles. Tap a booster in the tray (Fireworks, Needle, Sweep) then tap a target. A one-tap Undo covers the last move, accidental drops and mis-drags. Selling an item is a long-press then a drag to the Sell jar. Items of rare or high tier, and heirloom pieces, show a confirm dialog, with an Undo toast for 8 seconds. Adjacent items never auto-merge. Settings: left-handed layout, large-touch-targets, haptics levels, reduce motion, and colour-blind-safe patterns on every item tier (shape plus colour, never colour alone).
core_loop: Session (3-10 min). 1) Open the home screen and see the next story beat plus the current festival room to restore. 2) Enter a level. Each of the 64 handcrafted levels is a themed board with a preset layout, an objective (usually 2-4 festival orders), and a set of generators, crates and blockers. 3) Tap a generator (costs Spark energy, or free from a cooldown-only "hearth" generator) to produce low-tier items. 4) Drag two or more matching items together to merge them. A preview shows the count and result, and nothing auto-merges. 5) Combine chain items using recipes (cloth + dye = sari, ghee + flour + sugar = sweets). Merge 5 for a Big Merge, which skips a tier and returns a bonus item. 6) Drag finished items onto the order tray to fulfil orders. 7) Clear tangled thread, open trunks and use fireworks as the level requires. 8) Win: earn 1-3 Marigold stars (efficiency, no booster used, tidy board bonus) plus Lamps (soft currency) and chapter pieces. 9) Spend stars and Lamps on the Home: furnish rooms, light festival decorations, unlock the next story beat. 10) Return for the daily gift streak, the daily bazaar order, the heirloom collection and the live festival event. Session hooks: story beat every ~5 levels, a visible next-reward bar on the home screen, and energy regenerating on the local clock. No timers inside levels.

positioning: A warm, culturally specific merge game about restoring a grandmother's family home and bazaar, one regional festival at a time. Where Western merge games use farms and mansions, this one has diyas, silks, spices and sweets, plus a story about a family reuniting. Pitch: "The cozy merge game that treats your festival memories with care." Every promise is honest: it plays fully offline, has no forced ads, no gambling and no friend gates. The sensory hook is ASMR-friendly. Merges make soft clinks of brass, rustling silk and sizzling ghee, with clean short clips for social video.
progression:
Meta layers that give a reason to return:
1) Story spine: named characters appear within the first 3 minutes: Dadi (grandmother, the matriarch), Aarav (teen grandson who finds her letter), Meera (cousin, textile artisan), and Chacha Imran (neighbour, spice merchant). Goal: rebuild the family home and bazaar before Dadi's 80th birthday festival. A story beat every ~5 levels, shown as skippable text with optional recorded voice (original cast or text-only; never synthetic voices). Cutscenes and voice can be muted separately and skipped in one tap.
2) Home restoration: 5 homes and bazaars (one per chapter), ~12 rooms or stalls each. Spend Marigold stars to unlock each restore task, then pick from 2-3 decor options per slot (style choice, not power). Rooms become visibly alive (lights, animals in the courtyard only in the home view, never on the board).
3) Heirloom collection: ~120 heirlooms in sets of 6 (brass, silk, spice tins, toys, instruments...). They come from Big Merges, chapter chests with a visible 100% guaranteed contents list, and daily gifts. Each set completed gives a permanent cosmetic reward and a story postcard. Duplicates convert to Lamps, never dead ends. There is no random pack purchase.
4) Festival lighting: the home screen shows the festival progress; completing a chapter triggers a lighting ceremony (a signature moment, shareable as a short clip).
5) Daily gift streak: 7-day streak with a clearly displayed calendar. Missing a day pauses the streak (never resets) and a "Rest Day" is granted weekly.
6) Daily Bazaar Day: a single optional board with a small guaranteed reward, plus a weekly Festival Event (e.g. Diwali Week) running 14 days with at least 40% more time than needed. Events are fully finishable free and auto-grant all unclaimed rewards at the end.
7) Star goals and Chapter Passes: stars unlock a free milestone track.
8) Mastery: Collection book, board tidiness records (personal best), Big Merge counts, and a cosmetic profile frame. Opt-in: friend-compare leaderboards with a solo alternative. No social gates anywhere.
Plateau avoidance: after L30, the game adds side-branch "Heirloom Trials" and chapter replay with remixed orders so there is always a satisfying next goal. Paid shortcuts exist only as convenience; never the sole path.

level_structure:
64 handcrafted levels in 5 festival chapters, plus a post-game endless "Bazaar Day" daily board. Each level is a single handcrafted board (7x9) with a fixed starting layout, a limited number of generator taps (so the board cannot run dry), a deterministic produce table (no random dead-ends; pity logic guarantees the needed chain items appear), and 2-4 orders. There is no timer or move limit by default. Stars come from efficiency, tidiness and no-booster play, and 1 star is always enough to progress.
Chapter 1, Diwali Lane (L1-13, family-home courtyard): teaches merge-2/3, generators, crates, the order tray, the lamp chain (clay → brass diya → toran lamp → rangoli lamp), Big Merge (L8) and the Fireworks booster (L11). Story: Dadi's letter, the family promises to reopen the shop by Diwali. L13 is a boss-board with a layered order set.
Chapter 2, Onam Courtyard (L14-26): introduces Tangled Thread tiles (L14), cleared by merging adjacent to them or with the Needle booster. Introduces the recipe-merge system (L18): cloth + dye = sari, and flower + banana leaf = pookalam set. Story: cousin Meera returns from the city with a broken loom.
Chapter 3, Eid Night Market (L27-39): introduces Locked Trunks (L27), opened by a Key item from a key chain (brass → silver → filigree). Introduces the spice chain with a 3-input recipe (L31). Combines threads, trunks and recipes in L36-39. Story: the family reconnects with the neighbour who helped in the old days.
Chapter 4, Durga Puja & Pongal Pavilions (L40-52): introduces Sealed Clay Jars (L40: crack open when a merge occurs next to them, three-hit) and Festival Orders with multi-stage chains (L44). Introduces the Sweep booster (L47), which clears a row. Combines every mechanic so far. Story: the pavilion committee, a secret recipe, a rival bazaar that turns into an ally.
Chapter 5, Grand Mela (L53-64): the finale. Remixes all mechanics with twists: Thread-wrapped Trunks (thread over a trunk, L53), Chain Orders (one order feeds the next, L57), mixed recipe boards (L60), and a final three-room board set (L62-64). Story: the whole bazaar lights up, with the family and city neighbours together.
Difficulty rhythm per chapter: tutorial, 3 easy, a mild spike, a breather, a harder spike, a breather, a boss board. Post-game: weekly Festival Event boards, daily Bazaar Day board, and remixed "Heirloom Trials" (optional, no gating).
difficulty_curve: Difficulty is on a 0-1 scale per level. Ch1: 0.05-0.30 (tutorial and gentle ramp, a first spike at L8 Big Merge, breather at L9-10, boss L13 ~0.38). Ch2: 0.28-0.50 (spike L14 first thread board, breather L15-16, recipe spike L18-19, boss L26 ~0.52). Ch3: 0.35-0.58 (spike L27 trunks, breather L29, recipe-3 spike L31, combined peak L36-38, boss L39 ~0.6). Ch4: 0.40-0.66 (spike L40 jars, breather L42, spike L44 multi-stage orders, Sweep relief L47, boss L52 ~0.68). Ch5: 0.45-0.75 (twist spikes L53, L57, L60, finale L62-64 peak ~0.75). Rules: never more than 2 hard levels in a row; a breather follows every spike and gives a cozy reward; every 5th level is a story beat with a lighter board. Anti-frustration: a Hint toggle (off by default after first run), unlimited free Undo, an "I'm stuck" helper that is free once per level (shows a path, never auto-solves), and a generator guarantee so no level is unwinnable. After 3 fails on a level, a free Fireworks or Needle is gifted quietly. Ads and purchases never gate progress.
camera_orientation: Portrait, one-handed. The board is a fixed 7x9 grid (hex-free) in the thumb zone. The home and bazaar meta view scrolls vertically with a gentle parallax. Tablets get the same layout with larger margins.
market_opportunity: Merge is a top-grossing casual category with huge search volume ("merge games offline", "merge decor game", "cozy merge game"). Incumbents are Western or generic (farms, mansions, travel). The South Asian, SEA and diaspora festival theme is underserved yet emotionally strong, and festival seasons (Diwali, Eid, Onam, Durga Puja, Pongal) are natural live-event hooks and shareable moments. Competitor reviews show a wide-open trust gap: energy bugs, long unskippable ads, lost saves, undelivered purchases, board clutter and forced social. A game that fixes all of these can win ratings and organic ranking. Weak spot: the head keywords are competitive, so lead with the long-tail "festival merge", "offline merge" and "merge home restoration".
competitor_contrast: Versus Merge Mansion and Merge Valley: we offer an original cultural theme and recipe chains with a distinct logic per chain. Energy is generous and runs on the local clock, with a flat refill price. Ads are strictly opt-in and short. Nothing ever blocks a board tile: no roaming pets, no spawning chests, no ad icons. Cloud save and restore are visible from the first screen. Versus Homescapes: the meta is a family-and-bazaar restoration rather than a match-3 interlude, and the merge board is the main game. Versus Anna-style clones: original item chains, names, characters and tutorial, with no AI voice. Versus event-heavy games: every event is fully finishable free, never resets and auto-grants unclaimed rewards on end.
economy_monetization:
Currencies: Sparks (energy), Lamps (soft currency), Marigold stars (progress), Keys, and Jewels (a premium, light-IAP currency, used only for cosmetics and convenience).
ENERGY (Sparks): cap 100, regenerates 1 per 3 min using the local device clock (so 8 h offline = full refill, a pure local calculation with no network or update reset). A tamper guard uses a monotonic clock plus a saved wall-clock to prevent offline clock-forward abuse by capping credit to the cap and flagging only extreme backward jumps; honest time changes (timezone, travel, DST) are never punished. Generators cost 1-2 Sparks per tap; no item or action costs more than 5. The hearth generator (a basic one) is free with only a short cooldown. A level can always be finished on a single full bar. Refill price is flat and never rises: 1 refill = 20 Jewels, or free once a day via a rewarded ad.
ADS: rewarded only, always opt-in with a reward preview (e.g. "Watch ≤30 s: +25 Sparks, about 75 min of regen"). Close/skip control is visible; reward granted before the ad ends, and also if the ad fails to load (fallback grants it or offers a retry). Ad rewards are proportional to time cost. NO interstitials before L10; after that none by default. If ever enabled they are capped at 1 per 10 min, only between levels, never mid-merge, and never as a bait-and-switch (this is stated on the store listing). Max 1 dismissible offer per session, none while merging, no launch pop-up stack. Ad content is age-filtered (family-safe, no redirects).
IAP: Remove Ads (one-time, permanent, removes optional-ad nags and interstitials; rewarded ads still available as opt-in), Starter Pack (one-time), Jewel packs, Cosmetic Decor Packs (visible contents, no randomness), Bag Expansion (one-time permanent), and a Festival Pass with a free track that is fully finishable and a premium track of cosmetics. Convenience helpers (auto-group highlight, magnet) are free or earned in-game; if premium, one-time and permanent; never a daily subscription. Anything free is never later paid (grandfather rule). 
No gambling: no spin wheels, slots, blind boxes or paid random rewards. Any random-looking reward (chapter chest) shows its full contents and odds, has a pity timer and can never be empty.
Purchase integrity: server receipt validation, idempotent delivery, auto-claim on next launch, 'Restore purchases' button, an in-app receipt history, and in-app support tickets with a human first reply within 48 h, no auto-close until the player confirms, and replies in the player's language (English, Hindi, Tamil, Bahasa, Arabic at launch). Events: free players can finish everything; paid only accelerates.
Cloud save: Google Play Games sign-in prompted before L5 (skippable and re-offered), 'Restore progress' button on the first-run screen; saves include progress, purchases, heirlooms and event state, with conflict resolution that keeps the newest progress and never deletes. Apple platforms use the equivalent account.
technical_assumptions: React Native with Skia for board and meta rendering and Reanimated for animation; 60 fps on mid-range Android, 30 fps fallback on low-end
Cold start ≤5 s on low-end Android (2 GB RAM); crash-free sessions ≥99.5%; no battery-drain regression (frame cap, pause animations when idle)
Core install ≤50 MB; the optional art/audio pack downloads on Wi-Fi only and never blocks play
All levels, orders and meta are authored as bundled JSON data; deterministic seeded generator tables with pity logic; core loops 100% offline
Energy computed from persisted last-update timestamp, local device clock; verified by airplane-mode test for 8 h = full refill; no network check and no reset on update
Local save is atomic and versioned with migrations; cloud save via Google Play Games (Apple platforms use the platform equivalent); conflict resolution keeps the most progress and never deletes
Purchases via Google Play Billing with server receipt validation, idempotent delivery, auto-claim on next launch, restore button
Rewarded ads via a mediation SDK, max 30 s typical (60 s hard cap), close control visible, reward granted before end and on load failure, ad content age-filtered
Support via an in-app ticket service with human first reply ≤48 h, no auto-close, multi-language
Event system uses server-delivered config with a bundled fallback; events work offline for the content already downloaded, and unclaimed rewards auto-grant at end
Automated test harness checks that every qualifying merge increments quest, order and vault counters
Accessibility: reduce motion, colour-blind-safe shapes, scalable text, no flashing above WCAG thresholds, hints toggle off by default after first run

Privacy: age-appropriate ad configuration, no chat or typed text, data-safety form accurate; store listing says 'plays offline; internet needed only for cloud save, events and rewarded ads' (honest offline claim)
Content review: cultural advisors from each represented region review the art, names, rituals and text before release

No interstitial before L10; none during merging; at most 1 dismissible offer per session; no launch pop-up stack

store_listing_strategy: Title: 'Merge Bazaar: Festival Homes - Cozy Offline Merge'. Short description: 'Merge lamps, silks and spices to restore a family home. Cozy, relaxing and made for you.' Honest long description: 'Plays offline. Internet is only needed for cloud save, events and optional rewarded ads. No forced ads. No timers in levels. Energy refills on its own, even offline.' Keywords to weave in: merge games offline, merge decor game, cozy merge game, festival merge game, merge home restoration. Screenshots: (1) a satisfying big merge, (2) the restored home before and after, (3) the story cast, (4) heirloom collection, (5) 'No forced ads / Offline / Cloud save'. Run the pre-registration around Diwali and Eid with a respectful festival tie-in. Flag review: cultural accuracy, ad content filtering and the data-safety form.
